summary: On 17 July 2025, Genians Security Center detected a spear-phishing attack impersonating a South Korean defence-related institution. The message presented a request to review a military employee ID draft, used a sender made to resemble an official military address, and linked to a ZIP file named for the draft and the recipient. Inside was a Windows shortcut disguised as a document. Genians’ analysis shows that executing the shortcut triggered obfuscated commands and downloaded a purported military ID image and further malware from an attacker-controlled server. Metadata led Genians to attribute the image to ChatGPT, and its separate detector rated it highly likely to be AI-generated. Genians associated the operation with a North Korea-linked threat group through technical indicators. The published analysis describes the malicious execution chain and its capacity for persistence, remote control and data theft, but does not name an affected organisation, quantify data stolen, or establish that every recipient opened the file.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Genians reports that direct authentic-ID generation was refused but a draft/sample portrayal proceeded; its analysed PNG carries ChatGPT metadata and was used in a malicious ID-impersonation chain. OpenAI had published an applicable image-safety posture before the event. The prohibited-purpose condition was present in the resulting identity portrayal, yet the required protective effect did not prevent the output; the specific internal failure point is unobserved.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full current class review retains Required Control Activation at medium confidence: pre-incident provider policy prohibits fraudulent output use, a separate image-generation safety infrastructure was available, Genians observed refusal of direct protected-ID requests, and the ChatGPT-attributed official-ID draft nonetheless entered the attack chain. The exact internal subsystem is not a recognition requirement. Choice Agency Preservation lacks an AI-system objective and selected tactic. Identity-Representation Authority Separation lacks a materially identifiable real person’s likeness. Economic Solicitation Authenticity lacks a money or comparable economic-value request: this phishing lure sought malware execution and possible information theft. Source-Authority Separation lacks a downstream AI/governed system that obeyed the lure as instruction. The unmapped non-economic AI-mediated phishing mechanism is a taxonomy gap, not evidence that an economic recognition condition is present.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The AI Incident Database indexes the campaign. Genians is the originating technical investigator: it reports detection on 17 July 2025, reproduces the ID-draft lure and analyses the ZIP, LNK, downloaded PNG and batch/AutoIt chain. Its metadata examination links the PNG to ChatGPT; a third-party image detector returned a 98% synthetic-image probability, which is a tool score, not independent proof of every generation step. Genians reports that a direct request for an authentic military ID is refused, while a mock-up or sample framing can yield the sort of image observed. OpenAI’s March 2025 image-generation system-card addendum describes an operative safety infrastructure for 4o image generation; it is provider control-posture evidence, not a postmortem of this request. Genians’ later 2026 analysis links related infrastructure and techniques to a broader suspected APT37 campaign, but does not establish a later victim-specific loss for this July 2025 occurrence. The original prompt, model/runtime variant, account and internal control location were not published. OpenAI’s February 2025 misuse report separately establishes a contemporaneous policy against fraudulent or scam use of its outputs; it does not show how the July request was processed. The recovered image entered the malware execution chain after a recipient opened the shortcut, so the source does not establish that seeing the image induced the initial click.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The contemporaneous provider policy, published image-safety infrastructure, Genians’ direct-refusal observation and the ChatGPT-attributed official-ID draft used in the attacker’s chain support Required Control Activation at the governance level, with medium confidence. The exact prompt and internal control path remain unknown. Human operators chose the phishing pretext and malware route; no AI-selected influence objective is inferred. The current economic solicitation class does not cover this malware/data-theft lure because no payment, paid service or comparable economic transfer was requested. The human-directed non-economic phishing mechanism remains a distinct part of the occurrence. Genians recovered the image after shortcut execution, so its visibility to the initial recipient is not established.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The reported draft framing produced an official-looking identity artefact that entered a malicious phishing chain despite an applicable safety posture. The downstream human-directed lure sought execution of malware, and the current economic solicitation class does not cover that non-economic deception. The record keeps that deception distinct from the generation safeguard question.
